alhq.review:
I wouldn't recommend him unless you're able to give 150% of attention in his classes. Sir is very elderly so you might have trouble understanding his classes. That isn't to say he's not a great teacher. In fact he'll teach you theories from scratch and will take time explaining concepts thoroughly. He doesn't use slides tho. Handwritten notes for his class and he'll ask you to read specific topics from the book.
For assessment: 8-10 quizzes. He takes quizzes almost every week but will tell you the questions beforehand. So it's pretty easy to score full marks on them. And they're taken on a single topic. Not full chapters. One of the advantages of this is it helps to stay up to date with classes and it's a lot less pressurizing during mids/finals. He will count best n-2 or even more depending on the class performance. He usually discusses it by the end.
In terms of grading, sir used to curve by 10√x back in our time. I'm not sure if he still does that. But all in all, you'll have to have a lot of mental preparation to keep up with him if you take his course

mlm.review: He's teaching is top class. One of the best faculties I've ever seen. Very student friendly as well. Although his questions can be a bit tricky. But if you are regular and make notes properly, it'll be enough for you to get a good grade. He curves too. The course itself focuses more on concepts than mathematical calculations , so it's important to understand properly.

afrn.review: Easygoing. Not really good for learning tho. Gives MCQs in quizzes. And broad and short questions in mid and final. He provides some questions before the exam , and you'll get those exact questions in your exam. Pretty easy to get marks if you just study the slides. He doesn't curve . But he's lenient in marking. So, easy to get A/A- .

mth.review:
MTH sir is good. His teaching is very professional .Explains everything very clearly. He's very serious about class participation and interaction. And you have to be regular too. Because he notes everything about everyone in the class everyday.
His quizzes are easy. Mid and final questions are easy as well. The course itself is easier than MAT250 ,but the maths are much larger , so students tend to make silly calculation mistakes. If you can be regular and make notes and respond in class. You can do well in the exams.
One downside to MTH is that, his assignments are huge.
Good thing is that, he curves.
So, you can get a good grade if you follow his instructions and be regular.
